extracted.intended_audience: graduate students interested in weather, ocean, coastal, and Great Lakes resources and national policy decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Information and program requirements for applicants and finalists to the NOAA Sea Grant John A. Knauss Fellowship, a one-year paid federal fellowship that places graduate students in legislative or executive branch host offices in the Washington, D.C. area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience / eligibility (stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sea Grant’s John A. Knauss fellowship program provides a unique educational and professional experience for graduate students interested in weather, ocean, coastal, and Great Lakes resources and the national policy decisions affecting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is explicitly for graduate students with interests at the intersection of marine/coastal/Great Lakes science and national policy; the fellowship is named after John A. Knauss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and renewability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are one-year appointments and are not renewable; fellows receive pay for the appointment year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: matches nationally selected finalists with host offices of the Federal government located in the Washington, D.C. area for a one-year ... fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are placed in host offices located in the Washington, D.C. area; applicants should expect relocation/placement in DC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort structure — legislative vs. executive
rubrics_metrics.description: The class of fellows is split into two cohorts—legislative and executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/finalists are placed into one of two cohorts: legislative (work in U.S. House and Senate offices) or executive (placed in federal agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative placements (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, legislative fellows are selected to work in the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate. Fellows can be placed in both personal and committee offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative fellows may serve in either personal offices of Members of Congress or on committee staff; placements span both chambers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive placements (scope and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive fellows are placed in Federal agencies with marine policy-relevant missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of past executive placement hosts include: Committee on the Marine Transportation System, Department of Energy, Department of Interior, Department of Transportation, Environmental Protection Agency, Marine Mammal Commission, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, National Science Foundation, Oceanographer of the Navy, State Department, Smithsonian Institute, US Army Corps of Engineers, US Coast Guard, and the White House. This list illustrates the range of policy-relevant federal hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection / matching process (high-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: It matches nationally selected finalists with host offices of the Federal government located in the Washington, D.C. area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists are selected nationally and then matched with host offices; further details about the application process and alumni information are available at seagrant.noaa.gov/knauss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are subject to the availability of federal resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award and continuation depend on federal appropriations and available resources; applicants should be aware that funding is contingent on federal allocations.
